newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt outlines partial sell-off of 16 firms in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Egypt outlines partial sell-off of 16 firms in Q1.

text.p: The Egyptian state will sell off part of its shares in an additional 16 firms in the first quarter of 1997 to anchor investors or on the country's bourse, an official said on Saturday.
Mokhtar Khattab, advisor to the public entreprise ministry, told reporters that shares in seven of the companies would be sold on the stock exchange. They are:
Nile Pharmaceuticals and Chemical Industries - 20 percent to be offered in January.
Eastern Tobacco - 20 percent in February.
Misr Chemical Industries - 51 percent in February.
Egyptian Starch and Glucose - 51 percent in February.
Egyptian Electro Cables 51 percent in January.
Cairo Housing and Development - 51 percent in February.
Alexandria Mills and Stores - 51 percent in March.
Khattab said Egypt was seeking anchor investors in February and March for nine companies:
Steelco/Engineering Steelworks Projects
Metalco/Egyptian Metallic Constructions
Industrial Gases
Bisco Misr/Egyptian Foods
Chini/General Pottery and China Products
Misr Hotels
Nubareya Seed Production/Nubaseed
Simo/Middle East Paper
Delta Industrial (IDEAL)
Khattab also said the state would further divest shares in firms it began to privatise or had planned to privatise in the last quarter of 1996. These include:
Southern Cairo Flour Mills - 51 percent on January 7.
Egypt Free Shops, also known as Misr Free Shops, on January 12 and 13
United Arab Spinning and Weaving/Unirab - up to 51 percent in sealed bids on January 7 and 8.
Nile Cotton Ginning - 51 percent on January 14 and 15. Cotton traders and financial institutions may put in sealed bids for at least 25,000 shares.
